title: Bully: building an open world around bells, classes, cliques and a teenager's daily routine
summary: Rockstar Vancouver compressed open-world logic into a boarding school, using schedules, curfews, social groups and a gradually opening town to make a smaller map feel densely reactive.

sourceLabels.making-of: Inside the Making of Rockstar's GTA in Boarding School

blocks.text: A school changed the scale of open-world design

Bullworth is smaller than a Grand Theft Auto city, but nearly every space carries social meaning. A dormitory, classroom, cafeteria, gym and town shop are not interchangeable scenery. Each suggests rules, witnesses and expected behavior. Rockstar Vancouver used that familiarity to make short distances feel eventful and to build an open world around routine rather than constant vehicle travel.
The bell created a shared clock

Class times divide the day and give the player voluntary obligations. Attending advances minigames and unlocks practical benefits; skipping creates the risk of prefect attention. The schedule is simple enough to understand without a planner, yet it changes the meaning of movement. Crossing the yard before class is different from wandering it after curfew.

Authority figures react to trespassing, fighting, truancy and clothing violations. The consequence is usually pursuit or detention rather than lethal escalation. That lower scale lets misbehavior remain comic while still giving spaces boundaries. A prefect and a police officer belong to related systems, but the school context makes discipline feel personal rather than militarized.
Cliques turned pedestrians into a social map

Bullies, nerds, preppies, greasers and jocks have recognizable territories, silhouettes and attitudes. Story progress changes Jimmy's standing with them, so a route that was once hostile can become routine and then dangerous again. The reputation model is broad rather than individual, but it makes population behavior communicate the current chapter of the narrative.

English, chemistry, art, gym and other lessons use compact minigames rather than long simulation. Rewards connect the school day to exploration and combat: better apologies, crafted items, health or moves. Because lessons recur in escalating forms, the game turns repetition into curriculum. Failure remains part of the fiction instead of simply closing a menu.
The town opened with the school year

New districts become available as chapters advance, matching Jimmy's growing independence and widening conflicts. This gates production-heavy spaces without presenting an arbitrary wall. The player learns one social environment before receiving another, while bicycles, buses and shortcuts gradually alter traversal. Narrative structure and streaming scope support each other.
A dense cast demanded robust incidental behavior

Students talk, taunt, fight, flee, attend classes and react to clothing or reputation. Their routines are necessarily approximate, and repeated lines can reveal the underlying system. Yet the density matters more than perfect individual simulation. The player continually reads small confrontations that seem to belong to school life even when no mission is active.
Emulation should protect clock, audio and crowd stability

Tests should follow complete day-night cycles, cross class transitions, trigger curfew pursuits and revisit unlocked districts. Frame pacing can affect minigame timing and close-range combat. Streaming stutter is especially visible on a bicycle. Dialogue priority also matters because warnings, ambient insults and mission speech often overlap in crowded hallways.
Why Bullworth feels larger than its map

Bully's achievement is not square mileage but temporal density. The same corridor changes with class, authority, reputation and story chapter. A familiar institution supplies rules that players already understand, then the game bends them into progression and comedy. By making time and social role part of navigation, Rockstar Vancouver built an open world that remains distinctive without needing a metropolis.
